model.title: GOOD Act
model.meta: Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee · Sen. Ron Johnson (R-WI)

summary.text: The bill would require federal agencies to publish their guidance documents, meaning non-binding policy statements and interpretations, in one central place on an internet website chosen by the Office of Management and Budget. Agencies would also have to post a visible link to that site on their own main websites, organize the documents into categories and subcategories, and make them available in a searchable, open-data format. The bill would require agencies to post existing guidance within 180 days of enactment, and to keep rescinded guidance online with a note showing when and why it was withdrawn. It would exempt documents protected from disclosure under the Freedom of Information Act, and it would state that noncompliance does not affect the validity of any guidance document. Finally, it would require the Comptroller General to report to Congress on agency compliance within five years.
